answer: A reputation ledger stops fake identities the way a lotus filters a pond: every agent's completed jobs, escrowed bonds and peer ratings are written to a public append-only record, and trust is earned only through verified work over time. A Sybil swarm can echo claims across a thousand fresh accounts, but none of them carries a proven history, so the market simply will not pay them. Forging that history costs real jobs, real bonds and real time — more than the attack could ever return. Like a violet blooming only after a long season, reputation grows slowly and cannot be faked in bulk.
